---
title: "Memory-search models"
---

## Context Maintenance and Retrieval

[Ordinary CMR](models-cmr.qmd) learns associations between items and temporal context. Its factory combines two associative memories, a context, and a [response policy](components-response.qmd). The [model interface](typing.qmd#jaxcmr.typing.MemorySearch) describes the events that simulators and losses use.

## Semantic associations

The first recall uses temporal support. After that, the last recalled item cues semantic support for the next response. Two choices determine which factory to use.

| Combination at retrieval | Vocabulary input | Factory |
|---|---|---|
| Add semantic support to temporal support, then apply choice sensitivity | One feature vector per item | [Additive, from features](models-factories.qmd#jaxcmr.models.additive_semantic_cmr.make_factory) |
| Same additive calculation | Pairwise similarity matrix | [Additive, from similarities](models-factories.qmd#jaxcmr.models.additive_semantic_matrix_cmr.make_factory) |
| Scale the two sources separately, then multiply | One feature vector per item | [Multiplicative, from features](models-factories.qmd#jaxcmr.models.multiplicative_semantic_cmr.make_factory) |

## Emotional source context

Both models add support from temporal and emotional context when choosing the next item. They differ in what a studied item's valence initially cues.

| Model | Negative item | Neutral item | Positive item |
|---|---|---|---|
| [eCMR](models-factories.qmd#jaxcmr.models.ecmr.make_factory) | Emotional feature | Neutral feature | Emotional feature |
| [CMR3](models-factories.qmd#jaxcmr.models.cmr3.make_factory) | Negative feature | No initial valence association | Positive feature |

The [trial-input reference](components-factory.qmd) shows how valence and vocabulary IDs are matched to the model's item codes.

## Repeated presentations

[Positional CMR](models-positional.qmd) learns an association at each study position. If an item occurs twice, both positions can contribute to the probability of recalling that item. The response policy evaluates the available study positions. Positional CMR
sums their weights by item code before assigning item probabilities. In the
[blended model](models-factories.qmd#jaxcmr.models.blend_positional_cmr.make_factory)
each route first gives its own probability to STOP and each item. When an item
is recalled, those route probabilities also determine how much each route
contributes to reinstatement.

The [RepFR model configurations](https://github.com/githubpsyche/repfr/blob/main/repfr/model_registry.py) identify the reinforcement and reinstatement variants used in that project's comparisons.
